entry.title: Static HLS in git
entry.summary: HLS is a playlist and a pile of segments. Both are static files, which means git can hold them and a static host can serve them — no streaming server, no…
entry.content:
HLS is a playlist and a pile of segments. Both are static files, which means git can hold them and a static host can serve them — no streaming server, no account.

Why it works

A playlist is text. Segments are small, immutable binaries. Together they fit three ideas:

  • Segments never change once written, so they cache forever.
  • A playlist is a database list of names, and lists diff well.
  • Hosting is a git push away.

The catch

Binaries belong in their own repository, because about 46 MB per minute of video would otherwise sit in every contributor's clone forever.

  1. Keep text in the blog repository.
  2. Keep binaries in an assets repository.
    • Images in one repository.
    • Audio in another.
  3. Reference both with a logical asset: name.

A reference that names no provider is a reference you can move.

Here is the shape of a playlist:

#EXTM3U
#EXT-X-VERSION:3
#EXTINF:6.0,
seg-000.ts

Read more at the HLS specification and see the home page.

entry.title: Markdown is the format of record
entry.summary: A post stored as Quill Delta is JSON that only Quill can read. A post stored as markdown is a file that every tool in the world can read, diff and review.
entry.content:
A post stored as Quill Delta is JSON that only Quill can read. A post stored as markdown is a file that every tool in the world can read, diff and review.

What the editor may offer

The toolbar offers only what markdown can say: headings, bold, italic, code, links, quotes, lists and images. Coloured text would be silently lost on save, so it is not offered.

The test

md → Delta → md must produce identical bytes. If it cannot, the editor refuses to open the file instead of rewriting it.
